Status while the queue drains:

- **A sync from the live tree is running** (started 21:16, another session's). It began before the profile files landed, so its bundle won't carry the tower. I killed my redundant queued sync.
- **Two other sessions have sync + iPhone build-install pipelines queued** behind it, both from the live tree, which now contains the profile change. Whichever runs first will produce the right bundle.
- I'm watching two things: the running sync's exit, and the iOS bundle for the profile markers. When a bundle carries them, I'll make sure a build-install runs (a peer's if one is already going, otherwise mine) and confirm the install.

The iPhone is still on Wi-Fi. Plug it in when you can, so the install doesn't stall.
Watch is live: the live-tree sync (pid 39886) is still running, and a peer's Xcode build (48793) is in flight with the older bundle. Waiting for the sync to copy its bundle.

The web bundle with the profile tower and arrows is synced into the iOS project (and Android's assets). A peer's Xcode build picked it up as it started, and the build runner is now watching that build, will verify its product carries the profile markers, and will install it, or build itself if the peer's product falls short.

One thing only you can do: **plug the iPhone into the cable.** It's still on Wi-Fi, and the runner will hold the install until it reads as wired. I'll report the installed build when it lands.

Build runner reported interim status and paused, so I'm watching the peer's build directly now: it's a few minutes in, its sync produced the bundle with all four profile markers, and the phone is still on Wi-Fi. I'll report once the build ends and the install either lands or waits on the cable.
Waiting on the peer build (started 21:39). Nothing to do until it ends.

The peer's build failed at 21:48 with Xcode's "build operation failed without specifying any errors" signature, the same environment failure seen earlier today (process count is 760 of 2,784, so not a real limit; it's build-service contention). Its partial product did carry the right bundle, so the tree is fine.

The build runner is now queued to build it properly: it waits for the sync currently running from the live tree to finish, confirms the bundle markers, builds, retries once if the same environment failure recurs, and installs once the phone reads as wired. **The iPhone is still on Wi-Fi; plug in the cable when you can.** I'll report when the install lands.
plugged in

Wired now, confirmed at 21:51. The build runner will see that when it reaches the install step, so nothing more is needed from you. The sync it's waiting on is 10 minutes in; the build starts when it exits, then roughly 10 to 25 minutes to build and a minute to install. I'll report when it lands.

Update: the first build runner turned out to still be active and had already started its own clean build at 21:51:56 (`ios-iphone-20260904-215142`) with the marker-carrying bundle, so I stopped the second runner to avoid a duplicate 20-minute build. The phone is wired, so that build's install should go straight through. I'm watching the build independently and will report when the new app container appears on the phone.

The build blocker is a peer session's in-flight native work: a new Swift file, `PoplurAnalyticsRelay.swift` (Firebase Analytics), was half-written at 21:54 and broke both builds, along with edits in three other Swift files and the project file that depend on it. That's a real compile error, not the environment. As of 21:56:33 the file parses again, so the peer is finishing it.

Plan: a peer's build started at 21:54:54 is running against that tree now. If it compiles and installs, the profile bundle ships with it, and I'll confirm the new app container. If it fails on the still-moving native work, I'll build the moment the tree parses with no build running. The phone stays wired, nothing needed from you.

Good news from both watchers: the peer's build (started 21:54) hadn't reached Swift compilation when the analytics file was fixed at 21:56, so it's compiling the corrected tree with the profile bundle `index-BsxGDAIs.js` inside. Its script installs automatically at the end, and the phone is wired. Waiting for it to finish.
Peer build is 8 minutes in, past the asset catalog and compiling app Swift with zero errors, so it's beyond where the earlier builds died. Still waiting on its link and install.
The peer's build process just ended and another Xcode build has started in its place. Waiting for the result readout on the finished one before deciding anything.

The peer's build succeeded at 22:04 with the profile bundle inside (`index-BsxGDAIs.js`, markers present). Its script should now be installing over the cable; I'm watching for the app container on the phone to change.
Two more peer builds have started behind it. Not mine to manage; still waiting for the install evidence from the successful one.

**The profile change is on your iPhone.** Installed at 22:05 over the cable; the app container changed, which is the freshness proof since a web-bundle change never bumps the version string.

What shipped, per the build's provenance:

- **Build** `ios-iphone-20260904-215454`, from the iOS working tree at HEAD "Analytics: link FirebaseAnalyticsCore…", 1.2 GB app, Debug (stub binary plus debug dylib, which is normal for Debug builds now).
- **Web bundle** `ClayMapWeb/index-BsxGDAIs.js`, carrying the radius tower, the post arrows, and the radius-card recount key. It also still carries this morning's feed player.
- **Installed by** a peer session's pipeline whose build happened to start right after the fixed tree and the synced bundle were in place. My own build and one peer build before it died on a different peer's half-written analytics file, fixed at 21:56.

To see it: open Profile and watch the tower on the right rail climb to your total; open a post and use the four arrows under the left rail.

**Device status: 🔴.** iOS is done. Android is still pending: the A03 never appeared on USB tonight. When it does show up in `adb devices`, say so and I'll build the release variant and install in place.

One note for the peers' benefit: three more Xcode builds are queued or running from other sessions against the same tree. They'll reinstall the same content, so the app may restart once or twice.
